messages:
alex: Heads upwe've got customers reporting resume failures + unexpected shard hops after the CDN edge upgrade at 02:40. Console shows resumed sessions landing in different shards and duplicate resume_charge events.

jordyn: Can you share an example request/response? suspect Last-Event-ID handling?

alex: Example (client):
```
curl -i -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Last-Event-ID: evt-9876" "https://api.redwood.example/stream?tenant=acct-7"
```
Server trace (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-23T02:40:12Z] edge-cdn: incoming request, headers={Accept:text/event-stream}
[2026-03-23T02:40:12Z] edge-cdn: dropped header: Last-Event-ID
[2026-03-23T02:40:12Z] edge-proxy: assigned shard=shard-11 for tenant=acct-7 (no resume token)
[2026-03-23T02:40:12Z] stream-runtime: lookup resume token from Last-Event-ID failed -> new session created session=abc
[2026-03-23T02:40:13Z] billing: emit resume_charge tenant=acct-7 tokens=1
```

alex: TL;DR CDN stripped Last-Event-ID which the runtime uses as the authoritative resume token; without it we route to a new shard and count a resume_charge when the true client thought it was a resume.

cdn-team: We pushed a security header sanitation patch to remove unrecognized headers by default. Looks like Last-Event-ID was considered unsafe. Ops changed this at 02:37.

jordyn: Oof. Two problems: routing mismatch (shard affinity lost) and billing duplication. Impact: a handful of mid-size tenants saw a brief spike in resume counts and some resumed connections failing to reattach to their session-specific cache.

ops-bot: cdn-rollout v2026.03.23-37 -> us-east-1/us-west-2 completed at 2026-03-23T02:40:00Z.

billing: What's the safe mitigation for charge duplicates? We need to avoid retroactive billing changes without legal sign-off.

alex: Short-term mitigations:
- CDN: whitelist Last-Event-ID -> forward header (hotfix).
- Runtime: treat explicit Last-Event-ID header and X-Resume-Token query param as equivalent; if header missing but query param present, use that.
- Billing: add a dedupe pass for resume_charge events where resume_token matches an event_id seen within last 5s and origin shard differs. Flagged only, no retro billing rollback.

jordyn: Long-term: remove resume semantics dependency on a mutable header. Switch to opaque resume tokens that are URL-safe and sent in the query param or via websocket subprotocol. Also add signed resume tokens to prevent accidental loss.

console-ui: For Console: we can add a temporary "suspected-header-sanitization" flag on tenant overviews and a trace drilldown to see sessions that moved shards. That helps support triage.

cdn-team: We'll push a hotfix to stop sanitizing Last-Event-ID and add a config toggle per route. Rolling to us-east-1 now.

ops-bot: cdn-hotfix v2026.03.23-37a rolled to us-east-1 at 2026-03-23T02:52:14Z (sha: f6a9c).

alex: After hotfix, we re-ran a 500-conn canary: 0 shard hops observed, resume_charge deltas back to baseline.

billing: We'll keep dedupe-only flag in pipeline for 48h to gather evidence. If customers dispute charges, ops will provide trace evidence.

jordyn: Action items:
- cdn-team: add Last-Event-ID to allowed header set + config toggle (ETA 1h).
- runtime: add tolerant resume lookup that accepts Last-Event-ID or resume param and emit trace tag "header_sanitized=true" when mismatch detected (ETA 3h).
- console-ui: add warning badge + link to trace (ETA next sprint, temp banner now).
- billing: enable resume_charge dedupe-only mode for 48h (ETA now).

alex: filed INF-4550 with samples and affected tenant IDs. tagging support and legal.

cdn-team: notewe should add an integration test that ensures required streaming headers are forwarded through the CDN sanitize step.

console-ui: temporary banner added to relevant tenant pages: "We are investigating SSE resume anomalies caused by CDN header sanitization; charges are being monitored".

ops-bot: cdn-hotfix rolled to us-west-2 at 2026-03-23T03:05:09Z (sha: f6a9c).

ajordyn: Postmortem template: root cause = aggressive header sanitization at CDN edge removed Last-Event-ID used by runtime as resume token. Remediation = whitelist + token signing + console telemetry + billing dedupe policy.

alex: closing for now, will update when billing decides on final handling. Thanks everyone.
